title: Proper base change under locally closed restriction for continuous adic module sheaves
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ be a prime, and let $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its extended $\ell$-adic topology [def-weil-l-adic-numbers; def-weil-algebraic-closure]. For a $k$-scheme $T$, use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Define $\mathcal R_T$ to be the sheafification of the ring presheaf $V\mapsto\{f\in C(|V|,\Omega):f\text{ has locally finite-dimensional }\mathbf Q_\ell\text{-span}\}$, with pointwise operations and restriction by precomposition. Locally finite-dimensional means that every point has an open neighbourhood on which the span of the function's values has finite dimension. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a scheme morphism $v:T\to T'$, the coefficient map $\mathcal R_{T'}\to v_*\mathcal R_T$ is induced by precomposition with $|V\times_{T'}T|\to|V|$; module direct image uses this action. Its total right derived functor $Rv_*$ is computed in these module categories [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], not in a common-finite-stage category.

Let $p:P\to T$ be proper, where $T$ is of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism; def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $h:T'\hookrightarrow T$ be a quasi-compact locally closed immersion (a composite of an open immersion and a closed immersion [def-weil-open-immersion; def-weil-closed-immersion]). Set $P'=P\times_TT'$, with projections $h':P'\to P$ and $p':P'\to T'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. On $T',P'$ use the inverse-image coefficient rings $h^{-1}\mathcal R_T,h'^{-1}\mathcal R_P$ and the induced coefficient map for $p'$. The symbol $h^{-1}$ on modules means the exact topos inverse image with its transported action, without extension of scalars [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]; use its termwise functor on derived categories.

Let $M$ be an $\mathcal R_P$-module sheaf which Zariski locally has a finite partition by locally closed subschemes on each of which it is pro-etale locally finite free over the restricted $\mathcal R_P$. Then the canonical exchange is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(h^{-1}\mathcal R_T))$:
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{h,p,M}:h^{-1}Rp_*(M[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp'_*((h'^{-1}M)[0]).$$
Here $M[0]$ is the complex concentrated in degree zero. The exchange is the derived restriction map: its ordinary component $\operatorname{bc}_M:h^{-1}p_*M\to p'_*h'^{-1}M$ is adjoint to the composite $p'^{-1}h^{-1}p_*M\cong h'^{-1}p^{-1}p_*M\to h'^{-1}M$, with the last arrow the inverse image of the counit. If $\delta_{p,M}:(p_*M)[0]\to Rp_*(M[0])$ denotes the derived-unit comparison, then
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{h,p,M}\circ h^{-1}(\delta_{p,M})=\delta_{p',h'^{-1}M}\circ\operatorname{bc}_M[0].$$
No Frobenius structure, common open subscheme or compactification is part of this assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-finite-span-module-derived-comparison]. It identifies $A_Z=p_Z^*\underline\Omega$ with the specified $\mathcal R_Z$, matches the precomposition coefficient maps, and gives exact module equivalences preserving local finite-free trivializations and ordinary derived functors. Thus the given $M$ corresponds to an $A_P$-module $N$ with the same local stratifications.

proof.text: For each affine open $U\subseteq T$, [lem-sf-affine-proper-square-stratified-module] makes all four restricted corners separated finite-type $k$-schemes, both vertical maps proper, and $N_U[0]$ an object of the full ordinary bounded constructible category. These are exactly the geometric and coefficient-category hypotheses needed below; no separatedness of $T$ is required.

source.place: Definitions 6.8.3, 6.8.6 and 6.8.8; affine-square and finite-refinement lemma.

proof.text: Clause 3 of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational] at $\Lambda=\Omega$ makes the proper exchange on $N_U[0]$ invertible. By [lem-sfb-derived-exchange-exact-normalization] it is the ambient unit--square--counit map. On these separated corners [lem-sf-finite-span-module-derived-comparison] carries precisely this map to the sectionwise derived counit mate, which [lem-sf-ringed-restriction-exchange-open-descent] identifies with $\operatorname{Ex}_{h_U,p_U,M_U[0]}$. Hence that specified local exchange is invertible.

source.place: Clause 3; adjunction-normalized transport and resolving exchange.

proof.text: The opens $T'_U$ cover $T'$. The restriction equality and cover detection in [lem-sf-ringed-restriction-exchange-open-descent] now make the global specified exchange invertible. Its degree-zero comparison formula in the same lemma gives exactly the required equation with $\delta_{p,M}$ and $\delta_{p',h'^{-1}M}$. The coefficient isomorphisms in step 1 identify these actual inverse-image rings with those in the statement.

lean.statement: theorem proper_base_change_restriction {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (hc : ringChar k ≠ 0) (hl : l ≠ ringChar k) {P T T' : Scheme.{u}} [T.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (T ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [QuasiCompact (T ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] (p : P ⟶ T) [IsProper p] (h : T' ⟶ T) [IsImmersion h] [QuasiCompact h] (M : proEtaleRingModules P (coefficientRing l P)) (hM : ∀ x : P, ∃ (U : Scheme.{u}) (j : U ⟶ P), IsOpenImmersion j ∧ x ∈ Set.range j.base ∧ ∃ (n : ℕ) (Z : Fin n → Scheme.{u}) (i : (a : Fin n) → Z a ⟶ U), (∀ a, IsImmersion (i a)) ∧ (∀ y : U, ∃! a, y ∈ Set.range (i a).base) ∧ ∀ a, ∃ q : ((proEtaleModuleInverseImage (i a ≫ j) (coefficientRing l P)).obj M).LocalGeneratorsData.{u + 1}, q.IsLocallyFreeData ∧ q.IsFiniteType) : IsIso (properExchange l p h M) ∧ (proEtaleModuleInverseImage h (coefficientRing l T)).mapDerivedCategory.map (degreeZeroUnit (direct p (coefficientRing l T) (coefficientRing l P) (coefficientMap l p)) M) ≫ properExchange l p h M = ((proEtaleModuleInverseImage h (coefficientRing l T)).mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app ((direct p (coefficientRing l T) (coefficientRing l P) (coefficientMap l p)).obj M) ≫ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).map ((ordinaryExchange p h (coefficientRing l T) (coefficientRing l P) (coefficientMap l p)).app M) ≫ degreeZeroUnit (direct (pullback.snd p h) (inverseRing h (coefficientRing l T)) (inverseRing (pullback.fst p h) (coefficientRing l P)) (restrictedMap p h (coefficientRing l T) (coefficientRing l P) (coefficientMap l p))) ((proEtaleModuleInverseImage (pullback.fst p h) (coefficientRing l P)).obj M)
lean.note: The coefficient presheaf is already a sheaf, so coefficientRing represents its sheafification without changing sections. Restriction uses proEtaleModuleInverseImage into the actual inverse-image ring. The ordinary exchange is the mate of the section-normalized direct-image square; its derived map is constructed by rightDerivedDesc, and the main theorem includes its degree-zero derived-unit normalization. Supporting declarations are the constructions and properties explicitly used in this same node, not an arbitrary comparison datum.
